cases.situation: Two blocking wording linters use the same phrase inventory and error model; either result leads to the same action.
cases.expected: Classify the second path as duplicate-ceremony and recommend consolidation without weakening an owned boundary proof.

cases.situation: Unit tests prove component behavior, while one end-to-end test proves the irreversible user-visible property at the final consumer.
cases.expected: Retain the smallest endpoint proof because component success does not entail endpoint acceptance.

cases.situation: A very short skill omits its owner boundary and leaves two materially different routes under the same trigger.
cases.expected: Do not reward brevity; add or clarify the smallest route and ownership distinction that removes greater downstream uncertainty.

cases.situation: Two related reversible tasks share the same evidence and output; splitting them would duplicate context and add a handoff.
cases.expected: Preserve the cohesive combined route unless behavior evidence shows actual competition.

cases.situation: A reviewer sees repeated warnings but the intended reader, legal obligation, and risk owner are unknown.
cases.expected: Abstain from deduplication because the missing frame could reverse the preservation decision.

cases.situation: Two branches look structurally similar but respond to different externally observable hazards.
cases.expected: Retain the distinction or require domain evidence that the hazards can safely share one response.
